prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- Pick the platform that matches your trip style: Vrbo for full homes/families, Airbnb for unique stays and flexible hosts, Booking.com for hotels/instant booking and lots of last-minute options.  
- To find a good host: filter carefully, read recent reviews for patterns, check host profile/badges and responsiveness, ask specific questions before booking, and watch for red flags (no reviews, off-platform payment requests, inconsistent info).

Which platform is best (quick comparison)
- Vrbo
  - Strengths: Mostly whole-home rentals, family-friendly (large properties, pools), owner-hosted listings. Good for vacations with groups/kids.
  - Trade-offs: Fewer private rooms and unique “experience” stays. Fees and policies vary by owner.
- Airbnb
  - Strengths: Huge variety (entire homes, private rooms, unique stays), strong review system, host badges (Superhost, Airbnb Plus), good guest protections and messaging tools.
  - Trade-offs: Service fees can be high; host policies vary widely.
- Booking.com
  - Strengths: Very broad inventory (hotels, aparthotels, apartments), instant booking, often easy free-cancellation options and 24/7 support. Good for last-minute and business travel.
  - Trade-offs: Host interaction less personal for apartments; some apartment listings can be hotel-like in service.

How to find a reliably good host — step-by-step checklist
1. Define priorities
   - Whole home or private room? Family/kids? Pets? Workspace/Wi‑Fi? Flexible cancellation?
2. Use filters
   - Filter by entire place, number of bedrooms/beds, “family-friendly”, “self check‑in”, pet policies, and instant book if you need guaranteed booking.
3. Read recent reviews (most important)
   - Focus on reviews from the past 6–12 months. Look for repeated praise (cleanliness, accurate listing, check-in, responsiveness). A single negative is fine; repeated complaints about the same issue are red flags.
4. Check the host profile & badges
   - Prefer hosts with many positive reviews, Superhost/Top Host/Premier Host badges, and a verified profile. Check how long they’ve been hosting.
5. Look for detail and transparency in the listing
   - Good listings have many clear photos, full amenity lists, house rules, check-in instructions, and an accurate location pin.
6. Confirm practical details
   - Parking, noise, stairs, elevator, key pickup, check-in/out time, cleaners, Wi‑Fi speed, heating/AC, and anything special your group needs.
7. Message the host before booking
   - Ask direct questions (sample template below). Note their response time and tone — professional and helpful = good sign.
8. Check cancellation and fees
   - Compare total price (including cleaning, service fees, taxes). Note cancellation policy and deposit/hold.
9. Cross-check on multiple platforms
   - Same property may be listed across sites; compare total cost and terms.
10. Watch for red flags
   - No reviews, very new account with a great price, host insists on off-platform payments or direct bank transfers, evasive answers, inconsistent photos or listing details.

Red flags to avoid
- Host asks to pay outside the platform or to sign a private contract.
- No reviews or only one very short review.
- Reviews repeatedly mention the same problem (dirty, misleading listing, late check-in).
- Photos are few, blurry, or look staged and don’t match description.
- Host refuses simple requests (late check-in, extra guest) without reasonable explanation.

Sample pre-booking message to a host
Hi — I’m [Name]. We’d like to book [dates] with [# guests, children/pets if any]. A few quick questions:
1) Is the listed price the total cost, and are there any additional fees (cleaning, extra person, security deposit)?  
2) How is check-in handled (self check-in, lockbox, meet & greet)? What time is earliest check-in?  
3) Is Wi‑Fi reliable for remote work? Can you share approximate speed?  
4) Any rules about noise/visitors/parking?  
5) Are there stairs/steps or accessibility issues we should know about?  
Thanks — we’re respectful guests and can provide ID/verified profile.

Extra tips before you hit Book
- Prefer platform messaging (keeps protection and record).  
- Save screenshots of the listing and messages.  
- For long stays, ask for a clearer cancellation/extension plan and possibly a written agreement on utilities or maintenance.  
- If the property is very cheap relative to others nearby, double-check legitimacy.

If you tell me your destination, dates, group size, and priorities (family, pets, work, budget), I can recommend which platform and search filters to use and help draft a tailored message to hosts.
